title: Reality shows: Who is eligible to apply?
questions: Who is eligible to apply?
text:
Ideal cast members are:
* Business owners
* CEOs
* Startup founders
* Entrepreneurs
* Influencers with a business angle
* People actively building businesses, side hustles, brands, or ventures
There is no minimum revenue requirement.
Personality matters. These are reality shows, so we want people who are confident, interesting, competitive, opinionated, charismatic, or otherwise strong on camera.
The opportunity should also be financially appropriate. Someone should be able to comfortably afford the $20,000–$30,000 package plus approximately $3,000–$5,000 in travel/hotel expenses without expecting the show to immediately generate that money back. The generic travel/hotel budget is not proof every show requires a separate hotel: current show-specific housing guidance governs, including Mansion cast staying at the mansion during filming. Do not use the generic estimate to promise a travel allowance or require duplicate accommodation.
conditions: Source designated by project owner; preserve contract-dependent and provisional wording.

title: Reality shows: Is everyone guaranteed to appear in the show?
questions: Is everyone guaranteed to appear in the show?
text:
Yes.
Every accepted cast member is intended to appear in the series and is guaranteed to make it through the initial episode structure before standard elimination mechanics begin.
Some shows involve:
* elimination
* contestant voting
* challenges
* revenue/performance results
* judging
* team decisions
* other competition mechanics
The exact mechanics vary by show and may intentionally not be disclosed in advance. October 1 FAQ describes planned eliminations from episode 2 or 3 to seek more exposure, not an exact screen-time guarantee. VIP early-elimination advantage remains subject to challenge/participation terms; do not promise surviving the whole season.

title: Reality shows: What distribution is guaranteed?
questions: What distribution is guaranteed?
text:
This needs extremely precise sales language.
Based on what you described, the safe internal structure is:
Guaranteed:
* Inside Success TV distribution
* Whatever external platform your contract specifically guarantees
Not appropriate to promise casually:
* Netflix
* Hulu
* Amazon Prime Video
* Apple TV
* any particular third-party platform
unless that exact platform is contractually secured for that particular show.
I would not let reps say:
"You'll definitely be on Netflix, Amazon, Hulu or Apple."
That is legally dangerous if the actual platform has not yet been selected/contracted.
Better:
"The series is guaranteed distribution through Inside Success TV plus at least one qualifying external streaming/distribution platform as defined in your agreement. We also pitch selected original formats to major streamers and distribution partners."
Then separately, where truthful:
"Previous Inside Success programming has appeared on platforms such as Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV."
The distinction between distribution and being pitched to Netflix needs to be hammered into training. October 1 FAQ says the company plans submissions to Apple TV/Amazon Prime and cites a historical 99% success rate, but explicitly says placement is NOT guaranteed. Treat that as a source-stated historical claim, not a verified forward probability or contractual promise. Named platform guarantees still require the actual agreement.

title: Reality shows: Is the show REAL? Will it be hard? Can I get hurt? Will I lose money?
questions: Is the show REAL? Will it be hard? Can I get hurt? Will I lose money?
text:
These are real reality shows, no fake, so yes, there maybe harder elements depending on the show, participants have to be willing to commit to the process to make great tv. 
For example:

- KID CEO - The Kid is in charge of the business, and may make bad decisions that cost the company money, upset staff members etc, these cant be faked (but parameters are in place if they wanted to do something illegal or catastrophic, etc).
- ISLAND SHOW - Participants must survive and “rough it” - so yes, they may become hungry, sunburnt, dehydrated, have to walk long distances, physical exercises, etc - medical supervisors will be on site for support, and all participants have to sign waivers.
These shows aren’t designed to make the cast members suffer 24/7, its more to display HUSTLE, ENTREPRENEURSHIP, LEADERSHIP, PROBLEM SOLVING, BUSINESS, etc, but at same time, we do want some drama and wow moments to make good TV. Let’s look at the specific claim and the written details of what this includes.” For a prospect requesting other cast members' private contact details, Rudy's October 14 direction is to use the testimonial page on the main company website. Offer those public references respectfully; do not share private cast contact information or repeat internal disparaging language. Templates are in HubSpot. Opt-outs/no-further-contact requests stop further contact.
